response:
I recovered all 11 records and wrote them to `/app/recovered.json`, sorted by id.

**What was wrong:** the WAL file had been scrambled by XOR-ing every byte with `0x42`. I spotted this from the file header: a valid WAL starts with `37 7f 06 82`, but this one started with `75 3d 44 c0`, which is exactly that value XOR'd with `0x42`. The long runs of `0x42` (the letter `B`) were zero bytes scrambled the same way.

**Fix:** I reversed the XOR on the whole WAL file. SQLite then read it normally and `PRAGMA integrity_check` returned `ok`.

**Recovered data:**

| id | name | value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | apple | 150 |
| 2 | banana | 250 |
| 3 | cherry | 300 |
| 4 | date | 400 |
| 5 | elderberry | 500 |
| 6 | fig | 600 |
| 7 | grape | 700 |
| 8 | honeydew | 800 |
| 9 | kiwi | 900 |
| 10 | lemon | 1000 |
| 11 | mango | 1100 |

The WAL also changed existing rows: apple and banana now have the WAL's updated values, as well as rows 6–11 being added.

When my reading connection closed, SQLite merged the WAL changes into `main.db` and deleted `main.db-wal`. So `main.db` on its own now holds all 11 rows. Copies of the original files are inside the container at `/tmp/main.db.bak` and `/tmp/wal.enc.bak`.
